name: Purkinje fibre (conducting cell)
short_description: Heavily rebuilt cardiomyocyte of the ventricular conduction system: a fat, pale, glycogen-stuffed muscle cell that traded most of its contractile machinery for connexin-40 gap junctions, making it the fastest-conducting cell in the heart (~2-4 m/s) so both ventricles contract as one.

textbook.1: partial (gemini-3-pro-image; science correct - barrel-shaped conducting myocyte in an end-to-end chain, pale glycogen core with amber granules, two central nuclei in an obvious perinuclear clear zone, sparse myofibrils confined to a peripheral ring, teal connexin-40 gap-junction plates, endocardium above, thinner densely striated working myocytes below - and the muted educational palette with thin outlines is on-style, but the composition is a perfectly mirror-symmetric horizontal strip with a visible vertical seam splitting the cell's cytoplasm into two mirrored halves, and the cell bleeds off both side edges leaving almost no clean margin for leader lines)
textbook.2: pass (gemini-3-pro-image; re-prompted for a diagonal, non-mirrored composition and one continuous cytoplasm. Chain now runs lower-left to upper-right with large clean dark-charcoal margins at upper-left and lower-right for labels; the seam is gone and the glycogen granules and mitochondria are scattered asymmetrically. All reference structures present and correct: blunt barrel-shaped cell about three times wider than the striated working myocytes at lower right, pale cream glycogen-rich core, two central blue-violet nuclei with a clear perinuclear halo, sparse peripheral myofibril ring striated only at the rim, orange mitochondria, sarcoplasmic-reticulum tubules, connective-tissue sheath, teal gap-junction plates at both end-to-end contacts, endocardium along the top. No neuron features, no dendrites/axon/myelin, no full-width sarcomere banding, no text or border)

sem.1: pass (gemini-3-pro-image; used as final on first attempt. False-colour surface-only SEM of a chain of plump, blunt, barrel-shaped conducting myocytes in pale cream-straw with broad flattened end-to-end contact faces and fine blue-grey connective-sheath wisps draped over them; out-of-focus, distinctly slimmer and more strongly ridged dusky-rose working cardiomyocytes run behind and below for scale. Correctly shows no internal organelles and no cutaway, cool studio microscopy lighting, dark charcoal background, no baked text, no border)

3d.1: pass (gemini-3-pro-image; used as final on first attempt. Natural biological tints, clearly distinguishable and neither monochrome nor neon: translucent pale-blue sarcolemma with subsurface scattering, deep-rose peripheral myofibril ring showing rim-only striation, a large pale-cream glycogen-rich core dusted with amber granules, two central pale blue-violet nuclei each with a nucleolus inside an obvious clear zone, glowing orange mitochondria along the rim, pale sarcoplasmic-reticulum tubules, teal connexin-40 gap-junction plates at both ends of the chain, a translucent endocardial sheet above and slimmer densely striated working cardiomyocytes below right. Clean seamless dark studio background, no text, no border)

watercolor.1: partial (gemini-3-pro-image; full-bleed aged paper with a soft wash halo and correct anatomy, but the plate is laid out as a rigidly mirror-symmetric horizontal ellipse with two identical circular nuclei placed side by side dead centre, so the cell reads as a cartoon face rather than a naturalist plate)
watercolor.2: pass (gemini-3-pro-image; re-prompted for a diagonal, non-symmetric composition with offset nuclei of unequal size. Warm aged paper with foxing stains fills the entire frame corner to corner - no mat, frame, drop shadow or sheet-on-a-surface - with a soft grey wash halo directly on the paper behind the subject. Fine ink linework; pale cream glycogen-rich core with amber granules, two offset central nuclei with nucleoli in a clear perinuclear zone, sparse rose peripheral myofibrils striated only at the rim, orange mitochondria, ink-line sarcoplasmic reticulum, teal gap junctions at both end contacts, grey endocardial line above and slimmer strongly striated working cardiomyocytes below right. No text, no border)

reference: pass (Wikimedia Commons "Purkinje fibers 2.jpg", CC BY-SA 4.0, Alessandro Scalese - a real H&E light photomicrograph captioned "Purkinje fibers just beneath the endocardium". The field shows a row of large, rounded, conspicuously pale cells with clear washed-out cytoplasm lying directly beneath a thin endocardial band, alongside and visibly wider than a bank of darker, densely eosinophilic, finely striated working ventricular myocardium. This is cardiac tissue - definitively NOT cerebellum, and no cerebellar Purkinje neurons are present. Caveats: the raw download is a phone-through-the-eyepiece capture carrying a large black circular vignette; at this magnification the peripheral myofibril ring is not resolvable and the pale core reads as general clearing rather than a crisp halo; the species is unspecified and Purkinje pallor is known to be species-dependent. Cropped to the Purkinje row and cleaned with edit_image.py - vignette removed, H&E colorization preserved, no structures invented)
